handbookNote: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, interior section footers still read 'Version: July 2017', cover page dated 'Version: March 2025' reflecting Mississippi DPS's most recent republication date rather than any content revision), published by the Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- fetched directly from https://www.driverservicebureau.dps.ms.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/CDL%20Drivers%20ManualMarch2025.pdf (linked from the DPS Driver Service Bureau's own commercial-licensing page, https://www.driverservicebureau.dps.ms.gov/node/356) on 2026-08-22 (5.14MB PDF, 13 sections, full text extracted via pdftotext -layout to scratchpad/ms_cdl_research/ms_cdl_manual_full.txt, 9,577 lines); an older mirror of the prior edition (DPS%20CDL%20Manual_23.pdf, dated 2023-07 on the same DPS site) was also checked and superseded by the March-2025 file. Price matches this project's established CDL tier ($6.99). Real exam mechanics: the word 'Mississippi' does not appear anywhere in this manual's extracted text -- it is the generic unmodified AAMVA base manual with NO Mississippi-specific front matter, preface, or appendix of any kind (unlike, e.g., Kentucky, Louisiana, or Massachusetts's CDL manuals in this same project, which each have a state-specific preface disclosing exact item counts). Section 1.1.1 of the manual lists which knowledge tests exist (general knowledge, taken by all applicants; passenger transport; air brakes; combination vehicles; hazardous materials; tank vehicle; doubles/triples; school bus) but states no item counts, time limits, or passing-score percentage for any of them, and the DPS Driver Service Bureau's own CDL webpage (node/356) likewise discloses none of these figures. What IS confirmed: the federally standardized 80% minimum passing score applies to every CDL knowledge test regardless of state (49 CFR 383.135(a)). Multiple independent third-party CDL test-prep sites (epermittest.com, cristcdl.com, dmv-written-test.com) converge on a Mississippi General Knowledge test of 50 questions / 40 correct (80%) / 1-hour time limit, consistent with the typical AAMVA-manual-state format used elsewhere in this project, but since this could not be confirmed on any official mississippi.gov or dps.ms.gov source, it is explicitly hedged here rather than asserted as fact -- per this project's no-default-values discipline (AL, AR, KS, IN, ME, and MD CDL tracks in this project had similarly hedged item counts). What the manual DOES state directly: Mississippi's three CDL vehicle classes (A, B, C) and their weight-rating definitions; the six CDL endorsement types -- T (Doubles/Triples), N (Tank Vehicle), P (Passenger), H (Hazardous Materials), X (Combination Tank/Hazmat), S (School Bus); the ten standardized restriction codes (E, K, L, M, N, O, V, W, X, Z per the federal table reproduced in Section 1); medical/self-certification documentation requirements; disqualifying offenses and out-of-service violation rules; and the three-segment CDL skills test structure (vehicle inspection, basic vehicle control, on-road driving). Content-depth rationale: this manual uses the same AAMVA base content and same 13-section structure as several other CDL-track states already built in this project (Introduction; Driving Safely -- by far the largest section, split here into three buckets given its size and internal breadth, mirroring the Massachusetts track's split; Transporting Cargo Safely; Transporting Passengers Safely; Air Brakes; Combination Vehicles; Doubles and Triples; Tank Vehicles; Hazardous Materials -- the second-largest section, split into two buckets; School Bus; Vehicle Inspection; Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test; and On-Road Driving). Sections that are naturally short in this manual (Cargo, Doubles/Triples, Tank Vehicles) were sized down accordingly rather than padded to match larger sections, and the Licensing bucket is smaller than in states with a state-specific preface (e.g. Kentucky) since Mississippi's Section 1 contains only the generic AAMVA front matter with no added state-specific permit/retest/fee detail. Every question in this bank is grounded in a specific passage of the fetched official Mississippi DPS-hosted manual text cited in that question's source_note; none are invented, generic, or borrowed from another state's numbers.
